messages:
ashley: seeing a big spike in TLS handshake failures from ap-northeast edge since ~09:11. errors in front of cert-rotator services. 5xx and degraded p95 latency. anyone else?

karen: saw alerts too. routing telemetry shows decrypt errors from keystore fetches.

lee: can you paste the logs?

ashley: here's a snippet from the rotator logs around 09:12: ```ERROR rotator: fetchKey failed: KMS.DecryptDenied: access denied for principal service-account:cert-rotator-apne1
stack: github.com/redwood/rotator/keystore.fetchKey
 at rotator/main.go:243
```

sam: +1 that's an IAM/RBAC deny. we ran the RBAC tighten PR (org/iam#412) at 09:05—could be related.

maria: checked cluster-audit: there is a RoleBinding removal for "cert-rotator-apne1" at 09:04 by infra-automation. audit id: a1f3e2.

security-oncall: tagging incident. severity 2 for now. impact: failed rotations -> certs not refreshed -> backend handshake spike. potential for degraded traffic if not fixed in 30m.

lee: is this only ap-northeast? any other regions with similar denies?

ashley: only ap-northeast so far. eu-west and us-central rotators are fine.

karen: quick mitigation: grant temporary decrypt role to the rotator SA and re-run the job. we should avoid long-lived blanket perms.

sam: proposed quick allow: k8s RoleBinding create rotator-decrypt-temp -> ClusterRole kms-decrypt-lite for cert-rotator-apne1, expires in 1h. who can apply?

maria: I can apply now. creating a short-lived binding and will annotate with audit:incident=8421001234.

rotator-bot: deploy: rolebinding/rotator-decrypt-temp created in namespace=infra-apne1 by maria at 09:22.

ashley: immediate check: rotator started fetching keys again, handshakes dropping back to baseline. thanks.

security-oncall: good. next steps: 1) confirm why infra-automation removed binding (was it intended?), 2) add guardrails to prevent automation from removing bindings used by scheduled jobs, 3) rotate any keys exposed in logs (none observed), 4) postmortem.

sam: I pulled the infra-automation runbook: it prunes unused rolebindings older than 90d, but the rotator SA was incorrectly labelled and matched the prune filter. open issue: infra/automation#789.

karen: immediate follow-ups: - add whitelist for rolebindings named rotator-* in prune job - enhance audit alerting for KMS.DecryptDenied occurrences > 5/min - add canary test after RBAC changes to validate rotator keystore access

maria: logging action: pushed alert rule to prometheus: sum(increase(kms_decrypt_denied_total[5m])) > 3 -> pagerduty to sec-oncall + infra.

ashley: any sign of leaked creds? I grepped logs and S3; no secret material. only principal names and error traces.

security-oncall: fine, treat as misconfiguration rather than compromise. still run scoped key rewrap as precaution in 24h and include KMS audit logs in postmortem.

lee: for long term: rotator should have fallback cached copies for 5 minutes to survive short RBAC blips, and we should add a read-only monitor key for diagnostics that doesn't allow decrypt.

sam: adding to roadmap: RBAC safe-deploy checklist for infra-automation + a canary job that executes a mock decrypt against each regional rotator SA post-change.

maria: created infra/automation#790 with the prune whitelist change and infra/automation#791 for post-change canary. linking to the incident: https://redwood.internal/infra/issues/790

rotator-bot: job/rotator-schedule-apne1 restarted at 09:31; last rotation completed at 09:33.

ashley: monitoring: p95 TLS latency back to baseline, error rate normalizing. marking this as mitigated.

security-oncall: assigning owners: sam -> remediation/roadmap, maria -> short-term infra fixes, karen -> postmortem writeup and audit collection. deadline: postmortem draft in 48h.

karen: quick notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause (prune filter mislabel), mitigation (temp binding), config changes (whitelist + canary), monitoring (KMS deny alert), and runbook update.

ashley: thanks all. please add any missed items to the postmortem doc. closing thread once the postmortem link is posted. :white_check_mark:
